newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian 91-day t-bill yield seen steady at 7.02 pct.
newsitem.headline: Indian 91-day t-bill yield seen steady at 7.02 pct.

text.p: The yield at Friday's weekly auction of Indian 91-day treasury bills is expected to be steady at 7.02 percent, most dealers polled by Reuters said.
But some dealers felt the yield could fall slightly in response to Reserve Bank of India (RBI) initiatives earlier this week to trigger an interest rate cut.
The auction may see devolvement on the RBI unless non-competitive bidders come to the rescue, one dealer said.
Dealers said the 91-day treasury bill is very sensitive to prevailing call money rates. Call money rates were firm on Friday at 9.25-9.50 percent.
Other events which will be watched keenly by the money market on Friday include as auction of 14-day treasury bills and a four-day repo auction of government securities.
The 14-day treasury bill auction may not attract much response, some dealers said.
The RBI has maintained the cut-off at 4.96 percent at the last three 14-day treasury bill auctions.
"The market is in no mood to invest at this rate, given current call money rates above 9.0 percent" said a dealer.
A repo auction, also scheduled for Friday, would be keenly watched, dealers said. The last repo auction saw the RBI receive bids for 52.5 billion rupees of which it accepted bids for 51.5 billion.
Some lenders in the call market, who have locked up large amounts at the repo auction, may choose to roll over the money to keep overnight rates firm, dealers said.
Dealers speculated that the bulk of the 51.5 billion rupees accepted at the last repo auction was contributed by the State Bank of India, a large lender in the call market.
"It depends what they (SBI) choose to do," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "If they reinvest in repo, call rates may continue at current levels or may fall only slightly."
